jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Perception Engineer - Fallback Driving System
jobs.location: GM Automation - Sunnyvale - GM Automation - Sunnyvale
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.  
 
 Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.
 
 As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer   on   the State Estimation and Mapping (SEAM) organization, you will develop and improve the ML   perception   model that powers the secondary (fallback) autonomy stack for Super Cruise 3. You will focus on building robust   perception   from multi‑modal   camera , lidar, and radar data so the vehicle can safely bring itself to a stop when the primary autonomy stack is unavailable.   

You will lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of ML models for object detection, segmentation, tracking, and prediction, working closely with partner teams across   perception , planning, controls, and safety.   

What You'll Do 
 Design, train, and evaluate ML   perception   models for object detection, semantic/instance segmentation, tracking, and short‑horizon prediction using multi‑modal camera, lidar, and radar data.   

 Develop and   maintain   the secondary stack   perception   model that enables the fallback autonomy system to safely bring the vehicle to a minimal risk condition when the primary system experiences a fault.   

 Define clear ML success metrics (e.g., precision/recall, latency, robustness under edge cases) and drive systematic experimentation to improve model performance against those metrics.   

 Analyze large‑scale datasets, curate challenging scenarios, and build data   selection   and labeling strategies that improve robustness for long‑tail and degraded‑sensor conditions.   

 Implement efficient training and inference pipelines, including model optimization techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, distillation) to meet on‑vehicle compute and latency budgets.   

 Collaborate with software and infra engineers to integrate models into production systems, including interfaces, configuration, deployment, monitoring, and regression safeguards.   

 Partner with Safety, Systems Engineering, and Product to translate system requirements into concrete ML model requirements, metrics, and validation criteria.   

 Contribute to verification and validation strategies for the fallback   perception   model, including offline evaluation, simulation, hardware‑in‑the‑loop, and on‑road testing.   

 Participate in code reviews, promote ML and software engineering best practices, and provide technical mentorship to other engineers.   

Qualifications 
 BS, MS, or PhD in Machine Learning, Robotics, Computer Science, or a related technical field; or equivalent practical experience building ML   perception   systems.   

 3–5 years of experience developing ML solutions in   perception , prediction, and/or autonomous driving or related domains.   

 Strong experience with multi‑modal sensor data (camera, lidar, radar), including data preprocessing, synchronization, and fusion.   

 Deep   expertise   in modern deep learning for   perception , such as convolutional and transformer‑based architectures for:   

 2D/3D object detection   

 Semantic and instance segmentation   

 Multi‑object tracking and motion prediction   

 Proficiency   in at least one major ML framework (e.g.,   PyTorch , TensorFlow, JAX) and Python for model development, training, and analysis.   

 Solid software engineering skills, including experience working in C++ or similar languages in large, collaborative codebases.   

 Demonstrated ability to define ML metrics, design experiments, and systematically improve model performance and robustness.   

 Strong problem‑solving, communication, and cross‑functional collaboration skills.   

 Self‑motivated, with a passion for autonomous driving technology and its potential impact on safety and mobility.   

Nice to have 
 Experience deploying ML models on embedded or resource‑constrained platforms, including model optimization and performance tuning for real‑time inference.   

 Experience with AV/ADAS   perception   stacks, robotics, or ROS.   

 Familiarity with safety‑critical systems and development practices.   

 Experience with large‑scale data pipelines, labeling workflows, and experiment management for ML.   

Remote: This role is based remotely but if you live within a 50-mile radius of Atlanta, Austin, Detroit, Warren, Milford or Mountain View, you are expected to report to that location three times per week, at minimum.

About the Team   

 The Local Planner Controller team builds optimization-based planning and control software for GM’s Super Cruise system. The team formulates and solves online optimization problems that balance kinematic feasibility, collision avoidance, and ride comfort, and plays   a central role   in delivering safe, comfortable vehicle behavior through the Local Planner Controller and related guardrails systems.   

The Role   

 We are looking for a Robotics Controls Engineer to join GM’s Local Planner Controller team. In this role, you will work on challenging problems in trajectory optimization, vehicle dynamics, estimation, and closed-loop controls that support Super Cruise and other advanced driver   assistance   capabilities.   

What   You’ll   Do   

 Develop and deliver vehicle dynamics, planning, and   controls   software that supports safe and comfortable behavior in GM’s Super Cruise system.   

Implement, test, and refine optimization and control algorithms for trajectory tracking, constraint handling, and motion execution under real-world vehicle and environment limits.   

Partner with more senior engineers to break down ambiguous technical problems, evaluate tradeoffs, and translate algorithmic ideas into robust production-quality software.   

Contribute to technical reviews, code reviews, validation efforts, and day-to-day engineering execution using strong software engineering best practices.   

Work closely with cross-functional teams across   perception , prediction, localization, systems, safety, simulation, and evaluation to integrate solutions and debug end-to-end behavior.   

Improve software reliability and   development   velocity through testing, tooling, continuous integration, and thoughtful iteration on team processes.

Strong communication   skills and the ability to work effectively across disciplines.   

Passion for autonomous driving, robotics, or advanced driver   assistance   technologies.

Experience with model predictive control, constrained optimization, or trajectory generation for real-world robotic systems.   

Familiarity with ROS or similar robotics middleware.   

Experience developing or   validating   software for embedded or real-time control systems.   

Experience working with simulation, closed-loop evaluation, or system-level performance analysis.

jobs.title: Senior Virtual Hardware Model Engineer
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.   
 
 Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale. 
 
 The Role 
 The advancement of virtual tools has improved the way hardware and software can be optimized in vehicle design. As a Senior Virtual Hardware Model Engineer, you have the unique opportunity to shape GM's future by partnering cross functionally to develop models that unlock our ability to optimize design parameters within hardware components. In this role, you will lead development of select models in collaboration with suppliers, product development engineers, and other systems, software, and virtual teams.
 
 What You’ll Do (Responsibilities) 
 Develop high-fidelity component plant models in MATLAB/Simulink that mathematically emulate the electrical, mechanical/physics, and software interfaces of GVHE hardware components.

 Collaborate cross-functionally (Tech Specialists, DREs, VDDV, SIL, CoSim, suppliers) to understand hardware designs, control strategies, and boundary conditions, and translate them into clear modeling requirements.

 Implement plant models in a form suitable for use in GM CoSim environments (e.g., FMU export), ensuring correct I/O definitions, signal naming, and execution behavior.

 Use supplier specifications, design data, and physical test/bench/vehicle results to parameterize, correlate, and continuously improve model fidelity.

 Support integration of component plant models into larger system and vehicle-level co-simulation environments, working closely with simulation integration and CoSim architecture teams.

 Leverage plant models as virtual harness/component testers to confirm performance, run what-if studies, and explore fault and edge-case behavior before hardware is available.

 Document modeling assumptions, limitations, calibration parameters, and validation results to enable reuse and traceability across programs.

 Lead development and maintenance of model requirements documentation (Appendix C11, C12), with technical leadership in developing component plant model requirements, test needs, and deliverables are clearly specified and up to date.

 Contribute to standard methods, libraries, and best practices for component plant modeling within GVHE, mentoring peers and helping scale the capability across programs

 Own system-level modeling strategy across multiple components/domains (e.g., closures, thermal, chassis), including how component plant models roll up into integration/system models.

 Define and drive standards and best practices for model architecture, naming, fidelity levels, correlation methods, and validation criteria across programs.

 Lead model correlation and validation strategy: decide which tests/data are needed, set acceptance thresholds, and arbitrate trade-offs between fidelity and runtime.

Your Skills and Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Math, Physics, Computer Science, or other relevant degree

 Minimum 5 years of experience in product development, systems engineering, or work related to software/hardware connectivity. Preferred experience in translating physical phenomena into mathematical/Simulink models (electrical, mechanical, and software I/O).

 Proficiency with Matlab/Simulink or similar software that uses code-based logic for model-based simulation.

 Track record of delivering complex multi-domain models (coupled electrical–mechanical–software behavior) into SIL/HIL/CoSim workflows.

 Strong communication and collaboration skills

 Skilled and proficient with a variety of field’s concepts, practices, and procedures.

 Extensive personal experience and discernment to plan and accomplish goals.

 Ability to perform multiple tasks. Lead and likely direct the work of others. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected .

jobs.location: 2 Locations
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 
 Hybrid:  This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Milford Michigan 3-4 days per week, at minimum [or other frequency dictated by the business if more than 3 days]. 
 
 The Role: 
 General Motors is undergoing a major transformation, both in how we operate and in how we will influence the future of transportation in the EV realm. Our Software Services team is on the forefront of this work, emboldening our culture by seeking out determined, innovative individuals who will join our team to help move us forward and achieve our mission. 
 
 We are currently seeking experienced and motivated candidates for the roles of Battery & Propulsion HIL Engineer. The HIL Engineer role is responsible for creating hardware in the loop environments to enable development, model design , verification and validation of embedded controllers and calibrations for battery, electrification, engine, and powertrain. This position designs and maintains models using dSpace Simulink and Simscape tools. Simulation allows GM to move the integration and validation tasks earlier in the development cycle. It enables us to release new product and features quicker and to improve our competitiveness in the market. In addition, the position requires designing the harness, layout, the ECUs, and power for our HIL bench .
 
 You will be a GM Entrepreneur that is responsible to deliver finished products on time, meet goals, tailor our processes to be more efficient. You will utilize Agile principles, Scrum ART direction with stories written for tasks. These methods support Lean Manufacturing principles and DFSS knowledge to improve exponentially in what you accomplish and raise the quality in what you contribute to GM.
   
 What You’ll Do: 
 Work closely with software development, calibration, validation, and test-environment users to translate customer needs into testable system requirements and solutions.

 Create and maintain simulation models (e.g., plant, sensors and actuators, serial data communication, controller models) to build and enhance HIL /SIL test environments.

 Design , integrate, and support HIL benches, including harness design , power distribution, integration of key ECMs, and use of ISO SPI, CAN tools, and INCA.

 Plan, communicate, and coordinate test-environment strategy and model /hardware rollout to support applications and features requested by the user community.

 Partner with test-environment users to investigate, root cause, and resolve issues and unexpected test results encountered during test execution.

 Lead systems engineering activities, including requirements specification and balancing, functional decomposition, complex design analysis, and software anomaly resolution for current, new, and major programs.

 Provide, communicate, and champion common best practices within the software community; perform as Subject Matter Expert (SME) for at least one platform or application component.

 Apply Agile principles, DFSS tools and methodologies, and Lean thinking to continuously improve HIL engineering processes and daily work.

 Work with sources of models and equipment to ensure common models and other simulation assets are shared and reused across test-environment domains and architectures.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)​​:   
 Master’s degree in engineering (Mechatronics, Electrical, Software or Computer preferred).

 Bachelor’s degree in engineering (Mechatronics, Electrical, Software or Computer).

 4+ years of experience in design of models with real time simulation .

 4+ years of experience in HIL design , troubleshooting and integration.

 2+ years of experience in automotive engineering.

 1+ years of experience in applying DFSS tools and methodologies to solve problems.

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)​   
 Experience with developing microprocessor-based, real-time control algorithms and software in high level (Python, C/C++) language.

 Experience with embedded controls software and the automated software build processes, including gcc compiler, gdb debugger, Eclipse, and ETAS INCA measurement and calibration tools.

 Experience with commonly used HIL bench tools, such as ETAS INCA, Lauterbach, CAN (CANalyzer or Vehicle Spy), software code generation, Python, etc.

 Experience as a Controls, Software, or Calibration Engineer.

 Bachelor’s degree

You should be able to read and understand code (C++, Python), be experienced with creating and utilizing data visualizations, and have a strong track record of reliable, clear communication. You will lead execution across vehicle programs—triaging issues, driving containment, and ensuring long-term resolution—while using data, tooling, and structured triage practices to keep leadership and cross-functional teams aligned on software quality and launch readiness. You thrive in collaborative, high-stakes environments, exercise independent judgment, and can translate complex technical problems into clear actions for diverse audiences.
 
 What You'll Do (Responsibilities) 
 Act as a point of contact for AV diagnostic and AV Platform issues across manufacturing, service, program leadership and engineering. You communicate technical risks, resolution progress, and provide recommendations to leadership and release stakeholders directly impacting engineering priorities and release decisions.
 Define and improve triage workflows, enabling efficient and consistent issue ownership, classification, and prioritization across test and production environments.
 Track issue containment, escalation, and long-term corrective actions across the organization.
 Escalate and route failures to the right owners with clear context and expected outcomes.
 Leverage system and customer understanding to support prioritization across defects, technical debt, and future work.
 Lead root causing efforts, understand issues at a detailed level, and deliver both short-term containment and long-term solutions across vehicle programs, manufacturing environments, and release milestones.
 Perform deep debugging and root cause analysis across AV diagnostic and AV Platform software.
 Ingest, normalize, and correlate data from test benches, development vehicles, manufacturing, and the service community, creating large, useable data sets.
 Develop and maintain scalable tools, dashboards, and other data insight and visualization methods to identify trends, measure and forecast software quality, and root cause issues.
 Provide timely and accurate visibility into the state of the AVIP organizations released SW quality.
 Report on technical issues, translating findings and risks into clear communication for engineers, program stakeholders, and leadership
 Lead and support process improvements within the organization based on identified issues, continuously improving SW quality.
 Collaborate with adjacent engineering teams and downstream partners to address integration issues early and incorporate field and manufacturing needs into development and release planning.
 
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) ​​: 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, a related field—or equivalent experience.
 Demonstrated ability to lead and drive alignment across diverse stakeholders.
 Experience with observability, visualization, and data storage tools such as Grafana, Databricks, Power BI, GitHub, Azure, etc.
 Working proficiency in C++, Python and SQL for issue investigations, automation, and reporting.
 Analytical and debugging skills in real time distributed software systems (C++ and Python).
 Experience with the software development lifecycle, release processes, and software quality practices.
 A track record of strong initiative, judgment, and problem-solving in highly ambiguous, time critical environments.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills for data-driven technical storytelling.
 
 What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) ​: 
 Experience supporting vehicle launch activities and working with manufacturing plants and service or brand quality organizations.
 Experience with hardware and/or software diagnostics.
 Experience utilizing AI/ML or LLMs to perform log analysis, anomaly detection, failure clustering, automated summarization and tool creation.
 Understanding of vehicle architecture protocols and standards.
 
 Compensation:  
 The salary range for this role is $104,000 to $154,000. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Warren, MI three times per week, at minimum.
 
 The Role 
 Energy and Propulsion Systems research is aimed at driving propulsion and vehicle efficiency, cost, and performance improvements. Research also focuses on advancing vehicle and propulsion systems to target enterprise cost reduction through warranty improvement and engineering development efficiency.
 
 We are looking for highly motivated, technically exceptional candidates to join our team in the fast-growing field of Vehicle Health Management (VHM). This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of connected vehicles, data science, physics-based modeling, and advanced AI to create technologies that make vehicle ownership more convenient, and more seamless for millions of customers.
 
 In this role, you will help transform vehicle engineering data—collected through wireless communication with customer consent—into actionable insights that can predict system issues before they affect vehicle performance or disrupt everyday life. Our VHM work combines fundamental physics-based understanding with modern machine learning approaches, including large language models, to deliver scalable diagnostics, prognostics, and system performance management solutions.
 
 GM is a leader in this space. One example is the industry-first OnStar Proactive Alert for Starting System, which warns customers of a potential component failure before it becomes an emergency, turning unplanned repairs into scheduled maintenance. Today, this service is available on more than 10 million GM vehicles. Joining this team means contributing to technologies already making a real-world impact at scale.
 
 What You’ll Do 
 What makes this role especially exciting is the chance to work with a collaborative, forward-looking team tackling challenges in cloud computing, predictive modeling, and AI/ML to advance Vehicle Health Management. We are looking for researchers who are energized by technical innovation and motivated by the ability to translate their work into meaningful improvements in people’s everyday lives. Here are just a few of the opportunities you can look forward to:
 Generate innovative ideas and establish new research areas
 Generate intellectual property, document results, and publish high quality papers
 Develop next-generation technologies for vehicle system diagnosis, prognosis, and fault-tolerant controls as well as integration
 Develop and execute technical plans, including concept generation, prototype development, system implementation, and performance evaluation
 Lead technical discussions and reviews as an expert in this field internally and externally
 Maintain state-of-the-art technical expertise in related areas of responsibility
 Collaborate with cross-functional global teams and world-class universities
 
 What You’ll Need (Required Qualifications) 
 PhD in Electrical, Controls, Mechanical, Aerospace Engineering, or related field of study with demonstrated research capability or equivalent background, or Pursuing PhD in related fields
 Strong background in physics-based modeling for continuous and discrete systems, using first principles, system identification, parameter estimation, control and optimization
 Background in intelligent data modeling, using state-of-the-art AI/ML including LLM, signal processing, statistical inference
 Background in fault detection and isolation, diagnostics and prognostics, root cause analysis
 Experience in Python (including familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or Tensorflow), PySpark, MATLAB/Simulink
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills
 Excellent interpersonal skills to work effectively with GM internal and external partners
 This job may be eligible for relocation benefits
 
 What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 
 Industry experience in related areas
 Experience in application of advanced research and technology to the following automotive systems: internal combustion propulsion, high voltage battery, electromechanical actuators, power electronics, electrical systems, chassis systems, environmental sensors such as camera/radar/LIDAR, autonomous driving
 Experience in large-scale data analytics
 Hardware hands-on experience highly sought, including but not limited to experience in dSpace rapid prototyping, ETAS tools
 Experience of project management

Job Description 
 Our Mission: 
At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale 
 
 The Role: 
 As a part of this transformation, General Motors is investing significantly in Virtualization and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) technologies to enable early software quality in the vehicle development process.
 
 General Motors is seeking experienced and motivated candidates for the role of “ Senior Software Engineer - Virtualization and SIL Integration” to support development of virtual test environments in the Software-in-the-loop Agile Release Train (SIL ART). This role will support development of Level 3 vECUs, CoSim environments, and SIL processes for creating virtual test environments for various conventional (Gas/Disel ICE) and hybrid (HEV/PHEV) propulsion systems.
 
 This role is blend of Scrum Manager and CoSim Development Lead responsibilities. It requires technical leadership as well as hands-on SIL integration responsibilities. You will work with partners, end-user  and stakeholders across the company to deliver high-quality simulation test environments at various software and calibration development milestones. This position requires an individual with a passion for modeling and simulation of embedded and physical systems with in-depth knowledge of propulsion systems integration and demonstrated capability for managing a wide variety of technical and customer needs.
 
 What You'll Do (Responsibilities): 
 Create or utilize existing virtual controller models to integrate be used across different virtual simulations.
 Scrum Manager Responsibilities:
 Lead agile execution for the CPOWERSIM scrum, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, daily standups, reviews, retrospectives, and follow-through on committed work.

 Maintain backlog health, story readiness, cross-team dependency tracking, and escalation of blockers affecting delivery commitments across SIL ART.

 Coordinate work intake and scope alignment for new requests, releases, and updates across the scrum’s virtual asset and CoSim portfolio.

 Support Need intake and triage in alignment with SIL ART processes, where work is routed to the Scrum Manager and CoSim Dev Lead and reviewed through the ART front-door flow.

 Partner closely with ART managers, system architects, system engineers, software stakeholders, calibration stakeholders, and adjacent teams to align delivery scope, priorities, and timing.

 Ensure the co-simulation environments are delivered with high-quality and on-time delivery.

 Provide clear execution visibility on risks, milestones, release status, and issue resolution for the scrum’s products and commitments.

CoSim Dev Lead Responsibilities:
 Lead the development and integration of SIL co-simulation components to satisfy end-user testing and development requirements.

 Provide technical leadership for development of Level-3 virtual ECU and CoSim package delivery in the propulsion torque-controls space. Guide virtual ECU creation and maintenance HWIO/RTOS/Comms quality gating and review dashboards daily.

 Participate in the CoSim “Quad” meeting with the System Integration Architect, Product/System stakeholders, and calibration leads to identify SimBOM and virtual assets required to support SDV 2.0 TFRP testing requirements.

 Define requirements, evaluate gaps, and request needed simulation assets from partners across the enterprise and work with platform PMO to identify timing risks for deliverables.

 Guide technical planning and scope definition for CoSim package content, including virtual ECUs, plant physics models, sensors and actuators, and VIP/SDV interfaces.

 Create and maintain detailed documents for each release. Provide technical support to end-users for released SIL co-simulations and assist with user testing and troubleshooting.

 Lead debugging and resolution of systemic virtual platform testing and integration issues that impact quality or release readiness.  Drive technical reviews, prioritize defect closure, and ensure robust engineering decisions for model fidelity, integration approaches, and release content.

 Mentor engineers across the scrum, review technical work products, and promote disciplined execution, automation, and quality. Review simulations, user testing, troubleshooting, and issue resolution.

 Support deployment of SIL co-simulations for both local release and automation testing on cloud computing infrastructure.

What You'll Need (Required Qualifications): 
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Sciences, Electronics & Communications, Electrical, Mechanical, or related engineering disciplines.

 5+ years of embedded software development experience in automotive or allied industries.

 3+ years of virtualization, hardware- or software-in-the-loop co-simulation integration experience in any automotive integration or performance domains.

 2+ years coordinating agile development by leading a technical scrum, feature team, or integration team.

 2+ years of experience DevOps and CI/CD practices and tooling for version control (Gerrit, GitHub, etc.), build automation (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, etc.), binary release management (Artifactory, Amazon S3, etc.), and dashboard reporting (PowerBI, Databricks, etc.)

 Proficiency in Embedded C software development toolchain including GNU compiler(gcc)/debugger(gdb), Eclipse or VS Code IDEs and Python scripting for automation.

 In-depth understanding of automotive software standards and communication protocols such as AUTOSAR, CAN, LIN, SPI and automotive ethernet.

 Familiarity with software-defined vehicles architecture and topology, associated networking technologies along with measurement and calibration tool chains such as ETAS MDA and INCA.

 Strong familiarity with co-simulation standards such as Modelica FMI and SSP.

Preferred Qualifications: 
 Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electronics & Communications, Electrical, Mechanical, or related engineering discipline.

 2+ years of experience with modeling electric or hybrid propulsion systems models with a focus on torque controls.

 Experience with managing agile development using work management tools such as JIRA, JIRA align or Confluence.

 Experience with development and delivery of high-quality SIL co-simulation test environments, virtual ECU integration, serial data modeling, rest-bus modeling, sensor/actuator modeling for ICE and/or Hybrid Propulsion applications

 Familiarity with dynamical and mechatronics systems modeling or simulation tools such as Matlab, Simulink, Simscape, GT-POWER, Amesim, CarSim, etc.

jobs.title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer - Microcontrollers
jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 

Work Arrangement: 
 
 Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Milford, Michigan three times per week, at minimum.
 
 Our Mission: 
   
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.  
 
Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale. 
 
 The Role: 
 
 In-House HWIO (Hardware Input/Output) Team is part of the Mechatronics Software Platform organization, driving GM’s Software Defined Vehicle (SDV) strategy. We develop and test low-level embedded software that is portable and scalable across multiple automotive applications. As a member of the HWIO Engineering group, you’ll work with cutting-edge systems and designs, leveraging both AUTOSAR MCAL configuration tools and hand-coding in C.  A software developer in the HWIO team will be responsible for designing, developing, implementing, and testing the low-level hardware input/output (HWIO) software for various microcontrollers.  This means creating the best software solution with the understanding of requirements, microcontroller specification, and GM coding standard.  The developer will also make sure the solution is tested robustly by creating testing strategies and documenting the design.
 
We are seeking a skilled Senior Embedded Software Developer to design, develop, implement, and test low-level HWIO software for various microcontrollers. In this role, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams, create robust testing strategies, and ensure compliance with GM’s coding standards.
 
 What You'll Do: 
 Design, develop, and test low-level embedded software for functionalities such as RTOS, Memory, Fault Detection, Power Management, LIN, DMA, PWM, Discrete I/O, and Analog I/O.

 Utilize MCAL configuration tools or hand-code software solutions.

 Define and execute testing strategies to verify compliance with technical requirements.

 Perform independent code reviews and provide constructive feedback.

 Collaborate with teams across hardware, calibration, and requirements groups.

 Troubleshoot and solve complex issues with strong analytical skills.

 Document designs, test cases, and results thoroughly.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): 
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field.

 5+ years of experience in embedded software development (Embedded C).

 Expertise in AUTOSAR MCAL configuration and Complex Driver development.

 Hands-on experience with microcontrollers (ARM, PowerPC, Renesas).

 Proficiency with RTOS for multi-core systems.

 Strong understanding of schematics and basic electrical circuits.

 Experience with root cause analysis involving integrated basic and application software.

 Familiarity with debugging tools (Lauterbach, ETAS INCA, CANalyzer) and lab equipment (oscilloscopes).

 Ability to work independently under tight schedules.

 Excellent oral and written communication skills.

Job Description 
 Job Description 
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.  Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.  
 
 We are looking for a Principal Technical Lead Manager (TLM) to lead the Trajectory Generation team within the Embodied AI organization. This role combines deep technical leadership in machine learning and robotics with people leadership and organizational impact. Trajectory generation is one of the most critical components of an autonomous driving system. It is responsible for producing the precise vehicle motion plans that determine how the car moves through the world — lane changes, merges, turns, yielding, obstacle avoidance, and complex interactions with other road users. Every decision ultimately manifests as a trajectory executed by the vehicle.
 
 As the leader of this team, you will shape the algorithms and ML systems that translate sensor inputs into safe, smooth, and human-like driving behavior across diverse real-world scenarios. You will lead a high-performing team of engineers building ML-driven trajectory generation systems, and drive the roadmap that takes these models from research to production deployment on vehicles. This role requires someone who can set technical direction, mentor senior engineers, and lead large cross-functional initiatives, while remaining deeply involved in the technical architecture and modeling strategies. 
 
 What You'll Do:     
 Define and drive the technical vision and architecture for trajectory generation systems used in autonomous driving. 

 Lead the development of ML-based trajectory generation models capable of handling complex and dynamic driving environments. 

 Architect scalable training pipelines   using large-scale   driving datasets and simulation environments. 

 Guide the integration of trajectory generation models into real-time onboard systems with strict latency and safety requirements. 

 Influence the design   of next-generation   embodied AI architectures for driving. 

 Mentor senior engineers and help develop the next generation of technical leaders. 

 Raise the bar for engineering excellence, modeling rigor, and production-quality systems. 

 Foster a culture of innovation, ownership, and collaborative problem solving. 

 Lead complex technical initiatives spanning multiple teams across the autonomous driving stack. 

 Collaborate closely with teams   working on: data, perception,   simulation, safety validation, onboard systems.  

 Define roadmaps and priorities aligned with product milestones and safety goals. 

 Drive solutions from research prototypes through production deployment. 

Your Skills & Abilities:    
 MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or   related field.  

 Experience   leading technical   teams delivering production ML systems. 

 Deep expertise in   one or more areas: robotics planning and   control, imitation   learning or reinforcement   learning, generative   models, large-scale   machine learning systems 

 Strong software engineering skills (Python, C++, or similar). 

 Experience deploying ML models into real-world or safety-critical environments. 

 Demonstrated ability to define architecture and drive large technical initiatives across teams. 

Preferred Qualifications  
 Experience with autonomous driving, robotics, or embodied AI systems. 

 Background in trajectory planning, motion planning, or behavior modeling. 

 Experience   with large-scale   training infrastructure and distributed ML pipelines. 

 Experience   with simulation-based   training or evaluation of driving policies. 

Remote/Hybrid:   This role is based remotely but if you live within a 50-mile radius of Austin, Detroit, Warren, Milford or Mountain View, you are expected to report to that location three times per week, at minimum.  
 
 Compensation:  The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of the California Bay Area.  
 The salary range for this role is $296,300.00 to $423,900.00. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

 As a Software Engineer on the Software Validation team within the AV organization, you will play a critical role in simulation-led validation of autonomous vehicle behavior , with a strong focus on automation, internal tooling, and AI-assisted workflows .
You will leverage your experience in software engineering to convert validation strategies into well-architected, automated pipelines and tools that analyze AV behavior at scale. You will work with a team of engineers to define best practices, raise the bar internally on coding quality and automation, and evaluate the safety and performance of autonomous systems. You will be responsible for shaping the future of evaluation methodologies for AI systems and other ADAS features, architecting solutions that meet the testing needs of AI developers, systems engineers, and safety stakeholders.

About the Organization
The Autonomous Vehicle (AV) organization is dedicated to advancing the development of autonomous vehicles through cutting-edge simulation technologies and novel iterative development processes.
The Software Validation team focuses on unlocking software launches and continuous release decisions via simulation-led verification and validation strategies, prototypes, and protocols. Our collaborative environment fosters innovation and excellence, allowing us to push the boundaries of what is possible in autonomous vehicle testing.

What You’ll Do
 Design and deploy metrics and test strategies at scale to evaluate the behavior of autonomous vehicles in simulation and on-road.
 Translate validation strategies into production-quality code and automation pipelines that execute high-quality AV behavior analysis for continuous and scaled software release cycles.
 Leverage AI-assisted and agentic workflows to build internal tools and frameworks that make it easier to author, configure, and deploy metrics, tests, and validation artifacts.
 Ensure the quality and reliability of behavior validation outputs through monitoring, alerting, automated checks, and continuous improvement of the underlying code and data pipelines.
 Collaborate across teams to establish coding and automation best practices for the Software Validation organization; and understand stakeholder needs and translate them into robust tools and workflows.

Your Skills & Abilities
 Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science , or related fields.
 1–3 years of professional software engineering experience (including internships, co-ops, or research engineering roles) building automation, internal tools, or data/analysis pipelines. 
 Using large language models (LLMs) to summarize results, generate reports, or accelerate analysis,

 Experience working with large datasets to derive insights, build analyses, or drive decisions.
 Strong analytical thinking skills with the ability to interpret data and derive impactful conclusions.
 Ability to adapt and operate under ambiguity , going from quick code prototypes to longer-term, production-ready solutions on brief time horizons.

jobs.title: Safety Design Software Architect
jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 DUTIES : Develop the Solution Context and Intent at the Software level by defining requirements and communicating the solution vision. Analyze technical trade-offs, determine the primary components and subsystems, identify the interfaces and collaborations between them, define Nonfunctional Requirements (NFRs), guide Enablers through the Program and Solution Kanban systems, and work with Product and Solution Management, System Safety, and Suppliers to help ensure the allocated System Safety requirements and strategy are met. Provide technical training and establish effective mechanisms of knowledge sharing. Lead high severity safety-related investigations and work with other Safety Design Software Architects to resolve safety issues. Analyze the full control system and visualize what issues and faults can occur and build designs that mitigate those risks. Participate with system safety engineering in planning and defining high-level design of the product solution; explore solution alternatives. Operate within the business constraints when analyzing the impact of design decisions. Architect the solution for scalability, maintainability, and testability. Define subsystems and their interfaces, allocate responsibilities to sub systems, understand solution deployment and communicate requirements for interactions with the solution context. Derive lower-level system requirements from the System Safety requirements for function or interfaces. Support the ARTs during Planning and Implementation with technical guidance, review system architecture designs in all areas of ART planning. Assist in Backlog refinements to identify safety critical features and functions. Ensure proper prioritization of safety critical requirements. Ensure adherence to Development Vehicle Usage Levels (DVUL) and Automotive Safety Integrity Level (ASIL) requirements and timelines. Plan and develop the architectural runway for the SW Safety strategy. Create enabler features, stories aligned to program and solution roadmap and safety cases. Advocate for enabler requirements supporting the system safety strategy. Provide and monitor the necessary adherence to appropriate design guidelines for safety critical software. Support built in quality and continuous compliance. Perform software safety analyses based on derived requirements allocated by system safety. Establish system safety requirements generated by the above analysis or decomposed from the allocated System Safety requirements. Define safety critical calibrations jointly with System Safety and Calibration Technical Specialist. Participate in the definition of product development requirements. Ensure proper completion of all necessary business records and documentation. Participate and validate system demonstration adherence to system safety requirements. Prioritize, along with other Safety Design System Architects, the scrum team’s backlog.
 Define deliverables for scrum team development of system safety monitors. Mentor software and controls engineers into becoming capable Safety System Architects. Review system safety monitor designs and confirm overall quality. Hybrid Work Policy – 3 Days In Office, 2 Days Remote – Must be able to report to local office.

REQUIREMENTS : Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, or related field of study and Seven (7) years of experience as a Software Architect, Software Engineer, Project Engineer, or related role. Five years of experience with: C/C++ Programming and auto-code generated from Simulink models; Applying the dynamic system modeling principles and control theories; Implementing safety-critical design feature including redundancy and fail-safe mechanisms; Software-in-the-Loop, Model-in-the-Loop, and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Simulation; Algorithm development and calibration for Transmission controls; and ISO26262 and applicable FMVSS standards. Two years of experience with: Calibration and rapid controller prototyping tools; Simulink, MATLAB, DOORs, and GIT environment(s), and plant modeling and analysis tools; OBDII standards related to transmission; and Major automotive subsystems.

 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt.  Global Laboratory Systems Engineering (GLSE) is the team responsible for defining and executing developmental manufacturing and test solutions within GM labs and garages.  We cover manufacturing and testing projects across the globe with a constant focus on Safety, Quality, and Common data collection.  We strive to work seamlessly with GM Product Engineering, GM Manufacturing Engineering, GM Laboratory Operations, and strategic external suppliers to provide high value equipment and systems to General Motors. Our team covers a complex mix of projects and work, ranging in size and scope, both short term and long term. This results in countless opportunities to work with new technology and grow as individuals and as a team.
 
 We are seeking a Controls & Process Engineer to join our growing team! In this role you will be responsible for the successful implementation and validation of equipment and systems controls in new and existing applications. To accomplish this, you will partner with product engineering, manufacturing engineering, suppliers, and outside resources. Scope of work includes electric propulsion systems, battery cell manufacturing equipment, test measurement and control systems, PLC & PC software, and mechanical/electrical systems. You will develop and interpret standards, coordinate integration and installation of equipment and test systems, resolve equipment issues, support upgrades and improve equipment and test uptime, and ensure test data quality. In addition to controls engineering knowledge, an understanding of complex engineering theory and principles of mechanical and electrical mechanisms and experience in equipment installations and rearrangements are key to your success. Interested in learning more about this opportunity and GM’s path towards electrification and new cell innovation?

 Bachelor of Science degree in Engineering

 Ability to travel, domestic and international

jobs.title: Lead Software Controls Engineer - Transmission
jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Work Arrangement: 
 
 Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Milford, Michigan three times per week, at minimum.

The Role: 

At General Motors, we are developing   the embedded   software and control systems that enable advanced vehicle performance, drivability, and system integration. We are looking for a Lead Software and Controls Engineer to support new transmission controls development for a high-visibility vehicle application.   

In this role, you will develop, integrate, and   validate   software control algorithms that manage all aspects of new transmission operation while ensuring robust interaction with the vehicle and propulsion system. You will work closely with software, systems, calibration, validation, and integration teams to deliver high-quality embedded   controls   solutions that are technically sound, scalable, and consistent with GM software development standards and protocols.   

This is a lead individual contributor role for an engineer who can combine strong software and controls fundamentals with hands-on algorithm development, technical leadership, and disciplined execution. The successful candidate will help shape the software approach for new transmission controls while partnering across the broader vehicle team to deliver robust, production-ready solutions.   

What You’ll Do:  
 
 Develop software control algorithms for new transmission functions across the full range of operating conditions. 

 Design, implement, and refine embedded software to control transmission behavior, shift execution, coordination, diagnostics, and feature performance. 

 Integrate transmission controls software with vehicle-level and propulsion system functions to ensure aligned behavior and robust system performance. 

 Translate system and algorithm requirements into software functional requirements, software design content, and implementation plans. 

 Perform software design, coding, peer reviews, and change management activities in accordance with GM software development processes, coding standards, and software discipline expectations. 

 Create and execute software verification activities, including unit, SIL, HIL, bench, and integration testing as appropriate. 

 Troubleshoot software and controls issues, analyze root causes, and drive issues to closure across development and validation activities. 

 Collaborate with calibration, systems, validation, integration, and architecture teams to deliver controls solutions that balance performance, quality, maintainability, and integration needs. 

 Provide technical leadership in work planning, software design reviews, and problem-solving discussions while helping align the team on sound engineering practices. 

 Support technical reviews and clearly communicate software design choices, risks, tradeoffs, and recommended actions to stakeholders. 

 Contribute to continuous improvement in software reuse, documentation quality, test coverage, and consistency with GM engineering standards. 

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): 
 
 Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field. 

 5+ years experience in embedded software, controls development, or software systems engineering. 

 Proven experience developing software control algorithms in C, MATLAB, Simulink or comparable embedded controls toolchains. 

 Strong understanding of transmission, propulsion, torque management, or driveline controls development in a hardware-software environment. 

 Experience translating requirements into software design, implementation, and verification content. 

 Experience integrating embedded controls with broader vehicle systems and cross-functional engineering teams. 

 Strong understanding of software quality attributes and disciplined development processes, including change management and peer review expectations. 

 Demonstrated ability to lead technical work, influence decisions, and communicate effectively across multiple stakeholder groups in an Agile development environment. 

 Demonstrated ability to operate as a lead individual contributor with a high level of independent judgment and accountability for technical results. 

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications): 
 
 Master's degree in a relevant engineering or computer science discipline.

 8+ years experience in embedded software, controls development, or software systems engineering. 

 Experience with transmission controls, propulsion controls, or other performance-oriented vehicle control domains. 

 Experience with GM vehicle controls, calibration, data logging, and development toolchains. 

 Familiarity with software architecture, diagnostics, functional safety, cybersecurity, or software-defined vehicle development. 

 Experience supporting feature integration across multiple controllers or subsystems. 

 Experience mentoring other engineers and helping reinforce strong software engineering discipline and adherence to GM standards. 

 Experience with Agile CI/CD workflows, automated testing, or modern embedded software development practices.

Why Join GM   

At GM,   you’ll   help deliver the embedded software and controls that define transmission performance, drivability, and system integration in a demanding vehicle application.   You’ll   work on challenging technical problems, collaborate with highly capable cross-functional teams, and directly influence the quality and behavior of a critical propulsion-related control system.   

If you enjoy developing robust control algorithms, solving complex integration problems, and building high-quality embedded software in a disciplined engineering environment,   we’d   like to hear from you.

Job Description 
 The Role 
 Thermal CAE Engineer will be responsible for capturing information from a variety of sources inside and outside of GM Defense, building and running analytical models, interpreting results for customers, attending development team meetings, interacting with compartment integration teams and help to drive the design that meets internal and external requirements.
 
 Thermal CAE Engineer will build, run, and interpret results from various thermal models ranging in complexity from a single component to complex full vehicle systems. The engineer will be an employee within a diverse group of engineers supporting the virtual analysis needs of GM Defense. The engineer will be interacting with the GM thermal analysis groups, performing airflow and thermal simulations of varying complexity. The engineer will drive the design of unique vehicles and systems intended for government applications using virtual analysis tools.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Estimate propulsion heat rejection and determine air flow requirements for cooling system applications
 Size cooling systems and determine cooling capacity required and air flow requirements for system condensers
 Evaluate system exteriors with focus on cooling air flow and sealing using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models (front end cooling, passenger compartment)
 Evaluate propulsion systems cooling and AC system performance using various simulations tools
 Perform vehicle level CFD simulations to lead the design of the vehicle for thermal management
 Develop and support novel approaches for analysis in controls, thermal integration, and controls co-sim development
 Perform finite element and flow analysis on cooling system and plumbing components
 Pro-actively develop simulations for new programs based on vehicle content and functional objectives
 Post process and interpret simulation results to identify current performance gaps and develop solutions to improve performance
 Daily use of several commercial CFD codes, solvers and supporting software in Windows, LINUX/UNIX and HPC environment. These include ANSA, STAR-CCM+, GT-Suites, MATLAB SIMULINK, and other Internal Codes.
 Interface and collaborate with Studio and Engineering Teams, present numerical and visual data, and recommendations effectively, to ensure component and system level performance requirements are achieved
 Fully engage in vehicle development activity and proactively take ownership of simulation activity to best guide the design team
 Be willing to question the status quo and work to develop new methods and tools to streamline the defense toolkit in the thermal space
 
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering with coursework in Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer, Fluid Mechanics and Finite Element Analysis
 5+ years of professional experience.
 Experience and coursework in Lumped-Parameter Network Solvers, CFD methodology and application
 Theoretical background in propulsion plant modeling for controls algorithm development in GT-suites and MATLAB/Simulink as inputs to thermal model
 Experience with computer tools, 3D CAD files, CAE methods and Experimental Data
 Familiarity with Aerodynamic and Climatic Wind Tunnel testing, measurement techniques and data systems
 Experience using commercial CFD solvers such as FLUENT, STAR-CCM+, EXA-POWERFLOW, Mesh generators such as ANSA, HYPERWORKS and FEA Codes such as NASTRAN and ABAQUS
 
 What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 
 Masters or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering with focus on Thermal Sciences
 Mathematical modeling and analysis of various subsystems of both conventional and electric vehicle powertrain using state-of-the-art analytical tools, including STAR-CCM+, MATLAB/Simulink and co-sim environments
 Modeling, simulation, and validation of open and closed loop system models in desktop simulation and HIL hardware
 Adapt System models (e.g. MATLAB/Simulink ) for real time execution in a Model-in-loop, software-in-loop system
 Experience in design/release of automotive thermal systems
 DFSS training, Green Belt or beyond
 Comfortable with an ever-changing environment, flexible in skillset, willing to learn and can handle ambiguous assignments

Job Description 
 
 The Role:   
 We are hiring a technically opinionated Staff Engineer to serve as a founding member of the Hybrid Services & Reliability (HSR) team at GM. AV Core Infrastructure (ACI) is the core engineering organization responsible for the unified, secure hybrid platform that enables all autonomous vehicle hosting, validation, and testing. You will be responsible for the measurable reliability of the "bench cloud"—the end-to-end environment that flows from physical test benches through the secure cloud network into production runtimes. This role is on the critical path for Super Cruise, where the readiness of our hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) systems is a Tier-0 requirement for safety validation.
 
 What  you’ll  do   
 Reliability Architecture: Lead the definition and implementation of Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and SLIs for critical hybrid cloud services, establishing ready-state verification processes.

 Foundational Utilities: Own and automate core on-prem utilities, including DHCP, PXE, and NTP, to enable seamless server auto-provisioning and maintain a healthy fleet of remote CI-based HIL benches.

 Observability & MTTR: Develop and maintain dashboards and alerting to identify slot availability and system degradation, driving down Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) from high-severity incidents.

 Environment Integrity: Ensure uninterrupted data paths and dependency stability as data moves from ingestion at the test bench into the development and staging runtimes.

 Technical Mentorship: Act as a resource for colleagues with less experience, identifying opportunities to improve internal processes and services to support functional strategies.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)     
 Required: Extensive professional experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) with a focus on hybrid cloud platforms. Coding using Python/Go

 Required: Recognized expertise in Linux systems administration and the automation of foundational networking utilities (DHCP/PXE).

 Required: Deep experience with configuration management tools (e.g., Chef, Ansible) and Infrastructure as Code to reduce operational toil.

 Required: Proven ability to work independently on complex issues that require conceptual thinking and the wide application of principles and concepts.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)   
 Experience with Kubernetes (k8s) and managing hybrid service connectivity between on-prem and multi-cloud environments.

jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Work Classification: 
 
 Hybrid: The successful candidate is expected to report to Milford, MI three times per week, at minimum, or as dictated by the business.
 
 The Team: 
 
 The SDV Infrastructure Calibration Organization owns the delivery of foundational infrastructure calibrations across GM. We ensure vehicle platforms, domains, and software systems have the communication, diagnostic, and microcontroller calibration content required for safe, intelligent, and reliable operation.
 
 Our team works at the intersection of calibration, embedded software, diagnostics, communication systems, and platform execution. We support the infrastructure that enables software-defined vehicle capabilities to function consistently across programs, variants, and development environments.
 
 The Role: 
 
 We are looking for an Infrastructure Calibration Engineer to own the delivery and execution of infrastructure calibrations with primary focus on communications, diagnostics, and microcontroller calibration types. This role will be responsible for ensuring the right calibration content is developed, validated, applied, and delivered across vehicle and software programs with quality and timing discipline.
 
 You will work across calibration, software, integration, validation, and platform teams to support calibration readiness, resolve issues, and drive reliable execution across multiple builds and milestones.
 
 What You’ll Do: 
 
 Own the delivery and execution of infrastructure calibrations across communications, diagnostics, and microcontroller domains

 Develop, manage, and apply calibration content to support vehicle programs, cosim variants, bench environments, and SDV platforms

 Work across software, integration, and calibration teams to ensure infrastructure calibration readiness for builds and program milestones

 Analyze calibration requirements, dependencies, and applicability across programs and variants

 Support diagnostic and communication calibration implementation across protocols, interfaces, and platform use cases

 Validate calibration behavior through bench testing, simulation, cosim, and other appropriate verification methods

 Troubleshoot calibration-related issues affecting software behavior, communication performance, diagnostic execution, or microcontroller functionality

 Coordinate with SWILs, DREs, and technical stakeholders to ensure calibration content is aligned with software delivery timing and release readiness

 Document calibration content, execution workflows, assumptions, and known constraints for reuse and traceability

 Identify opportunities to improve calibration workflows, execution efficiency, and infrastructure quality through better tools, automation, and process discipline

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): 
 
 Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Controls, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field

 5+ years of experience in calibration, embedded software, infrastructure software, diagnostics, communications, or related automotive engineering work

 Strong understanding of calibration execution and delivery in infrastructure, software, or vehicle development environments

 Experience with vehicle communication protocols such as CAN, LIN, Ethernet, or related communication frameworks

 Familiarity with diagnostics concepts and tools, including UDS, GMW, or related diagnostic workflows

 Working knowledge of microcontroller-based systems and embedded software behavior

 Ability to analyze technical issues, identify root causes, and support issue resolution across multiple teams

 Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple calibration activities, priorities, and timelines

 Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams

 Ability to work independently and drive execution in a fast-paced environment

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications): 
 
 Master’s degree in engineering, computer science, or a related technical field

 8+ years of experience in infrastructure calibration, diagnostics, embedded systems, or SDV-related software environments

 Experience supporting communications, diagnostics, or microcontroller calibration delivery across multiple vehicle programs

 Familiarity with calibration automation, scripting, or software-driven workflow improvements

 Experience working with integration teams, software release teams, or build execution organizations

 Proficiency in Python or similar scripting languages

 Experience with simulation, cosim, bench validation, or automated calibration verification methods

 Strong ownership mindset with the ability to drive issues to closure and maintain execution discipline across complex technical work

Who Thrives Here: 
 
 Engineers who are detail oriented and strong at managing technical execution across many moving pieces

 People who understand calibration intent and can translate it into reliable delivery and application across programs

 Individuals who are comfortable working across software, diagnostics, communications, and embedded system boundaries

 Teammates who take ownership, solve problems quickly, and keep stakeholders aligned on timing, risks, and readiness

Job Description 
 Role: The Principal Software Engineer at General Motors should be an experienced leader who cares deeply about software and software quality.  As a Principal Software Engineer, you will be responsible for broad oversight and ownership of safety and regulatory design compliance for all features in the Body Controls domain across the subsystems of Occupant Protection, Occupant Position, Occupant Cabin Comfort, Lighting & Visibility, and Secure Vehicle Access. This responsibility will extend to designing, documenting, and guiding the implementation of complex, highly scalable, embedded software in C/C++.  Your work will guarantee that the continued evolution and innovation of Body Controls Software while sustaining a strong and forward-thinking compliance posture. 
 At General Motors, we believe in engineering leaders who remain deeply technical and understand the challenges their teams are facing. The ideal candidate will be comfortable switching context from programming in C/C++, designing elegant software architectures, defining how to test, benchmark, and debug complex systems, engaging with third parties (including standards bodies and regulatory teams) and providing mentorship for staff and senior software engineers.
 
 What you’ll do: 
 Define and lead software compliance strategy for new technology and highly complex features for Body Controls Platform development with a focus on Occupant Protection, Occupant Position, Occupant Cabin Comfort, Lighting & Visibility, Secure Vehicle Access, and abstraction layers
 Define a compliance & technology roadmap
 Drive architecture standards, patterns, and principles, actively engaging with and leading third party standards initiatives
 Serve as subject matter expert on analyzing, judging, and advising on disposition of technical matters related to safety, regulation and compliance
 Establish a forward looking external posture on emerging trends and standards impacting the Body Controls domains
 Work across orgs to ensure that the joint architecture across the full stack is coherent and can solve relevant problems
 Maintain alignment between senior leadership and engineering teams through effective executive communication
 Maintain high-quality bar in projects from the start and champion quality improvements by implementing better technical practices
 Work with other teams to ensure the system level architecture and strategies for compliance are implemented
 Initiate large projects with complex architecture, breaking it down to the right logical components so others can be utilized effectively
 Improve and deliver reliable software through requirements generation, continuous integration, automated testing, issue tracking, and code reviews
 Provide technical leadership, guidance and mentorship to Senior and Staff engineers as they propose, prototype, evaluate, and iterate solutions, as well as through their career progression
 Lead large initiatives involving many stakeholders by driving impact analysis, and ensuring alignment with the larger architectural roadmap
 
 Your Skills & Abilities: 
 Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electronics & Communication, Electrical Engineering, or related degree
 10+ years of experience in Embedded Software development and launching quality software into production
 Demonstrated successful technical track record leading software development teams in complex system environments
 Experience with safety critical development and testing in regulated environments (examples include FDA, FAA, Automotive, Aerospace)

 Experience leading external standards committees

 Experience with embedded build systems, CI/CD and test automation

jobs.location: Markham, Ontario, Canada
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Vacancy Status: 
 
 This posting is not for an existing vacancy within the organization and is open to new applications. (New Head Count)
 
 AI Disclosure: 
 As part of the application process, Artificial Intelligence will be used in the hiring process for this role
 
 Hybrid: 
 
 This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Markham three times per week, at minimum [or other frequency dictated by the business].
 
 About The Role: 
 
General Motors is transforming how we develop and validate embedded controls and software as we move toward our Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions, Zero Congestion vision. We are seeking a Staff Software Architect – Mechatronics Controls Simulation to lead the technical architecture of simulation environments supporting GM’s Vehicle Body Controls domain (vehicle access, cabin thermal, occupant positioning, occupant protection, lighting, visibility, vehicle state, and related functions) within the Virtualization & SIL Integration (VnSI) organization.
 
 In this role, you will own the end-to-end simulation architecture for the Vehicle Body Controls domain, define and govern CoSim packages, and lead variant and configuration management across programs and model years. You will partner closely with Simulation Integration Engineers (SIEs), System Integration Architects, Software Architects, and SW Quality Architects to ensure our simulation solutions are scalable, robust, and fully integrated into continuous integration (CI) pipelines for GM’s Software Defined Vehicle (SDV) Architecture.
 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Provide technical and architectural leadership for the Vehicle Body
Controls domain simulation, setting the long-term vision and roadmap for
simulation capabilities and infrastructure.
 Define and maintain the simulation architecture for the Vehicle Body
Controls domain, addressing functional and non-functional requirements
(performance, fidelity, scalability, reusability, maintainability) and align
with SDV and Mechatronics Infrastructure direction.
 Define the variant and configuration management strategy for simulation
packages across programs, regions, model years, and option content (e.g.,
trim levels, content packages, regulatory variants).
  Collaborate with System Engineers and SIEs to define Simulation Bills of
Materials (SIMBOMs) that map program test requirements and feature
content into concrete CoSim assets for each configuration.
 Establish and maintain standards for simulation package structure,
documentation, versioning, and release notes to ensure traceability and
ease of deployment across virtual test environments and CI pipelines.
 Own the simulation architecture for behavioral modeling for systems
outside of the test boundary, defining how networks, ECUs, and vehicle
behaviors are represented in simulation.
 Define the architectural strategy and technical enablers required to scale
CI/CD across simulation packages, virtual ECUs, and test environments.
  Partner with pipeline and tools teams to align test packages with CI quality
gates (e.g., build, smoke tests, regression suites, coverage criteria) and
ensure failures are actionable by teams.
 Establish architecture governance processes, conduct design reviews, and
drive alignment across simulation, software, and systems engineering
organizations.
 Contribute to, and in some cases lead, training and lunch-and-learn
sessions on simulation architecture, simulation packaging, configuration
management, and CI practices.

 Basic Qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Electrical / Computer / Mechatronics Engineering,
Computer Science, or related field.
 8+ years of relevant experience in embedded software, systems
engineering, or controls, with substantial time spent on simulation,
SIL/HIL, or co-simulation for automotive or similar safety-critical domains.
 Strong skills in at least one software language used in simulation tooling
(e.g., C/C++, Python) and experience working with automated build and CI
tools (e.g., Git, GitHub Actions, gcc/gdb, Eclipse or similar).
 Proven experience as a Systems Architect, Software/System Engineer, or
simulation technical lead with responsibility for architecture across
multiple programs or domains.
  Deep hands-on experience with test environments, including integration of
controls, plant models, and communication models for embedded
controllers.
 Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional technical discussions, drive
consensus, and make trade-offs across performance, quality, and delivery.
Preferred Qualifications
 Master’s or PhD degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related
field.
  Prior Staff-level (or equivalent) experience defining and leading the
architecture of complex embedded or simulation systems that span
multiple Electronic Control Units (ECUs), vehicle domains, and feature sets.
  Experience designing or operating continuous integration pipelines for
embedded software, including quality gates, promotion strategies, and
automated regression selection.
 Proficiency with MATLAB/Simulink for plant and/or behavior model
development and integration, and familiarity with FMU/FMI and SSP
standards.
 Solid knowledge of automotive communication technologies (CAN, LIN,
automotive Ethernet) and experience modeling or configuring network
behavior in simulation.
 Hands-on experience designing or leading variant and configuration
management strategies for embedded software, simulation, or test
environments.
 Familiarity with AUTOSAR layered software architecture and integration of
AUTOSAR-based ECUs into CoSim environments.
  Experience with cloud-hosted simulation / virtualization platforms and
scaling test execution on shared infrastructure.
